I keep seeing things about GamerGate and feminists and video games, but I really have no idea what it is or how it started.
Sadly, this is one of the better articles describing it https://encyclopediadramatica.se/Gamergate

Basically, in 2014, some people were concerned about allegedly crummy ethics in gaming journalism, such as claims that a game developer named Zoë Quinn was given positive coverage by her then-boyfriend, an editor at Kotaku. The people criticizing gaming journalism ethics branded their cause "Gamergate" (a la "Watergate") to describe the alleged scandal.

Then, to make a long and clusterfucky story short, feminists and other so-called "social justice warriors" (SJWs) became convinced that the Gamergate movement was actually rooted in sexism. The anti-Gamergaters (feminists, etc.) believed that Gamergaters were misogynists who didn't like that women are increasingly trying to partake in a traditionally male-dominated hobby. They evidenced alleged death threats and rape threats as proof of the true motives of Gamergaters.

Soon, along came one Anita Sarkeesian, a young hardcore staunch feminist/SJW who started a Kickstarter fundraiser to fund a series of videos called Tropes vs. Women in Video Games that she claimed would investigate sexism in video games. She raised a six-figure dollar amount from her campaign but notoriously failed to deliver on her Kickstarter's promised schedule for video content.

At this point, the origins of Gamergate as a rebuke of shoddy journalism ethics became increasingly irrelevant as the battlefield shifted to that of feminism/SJWism in general, who Gamergaters became fed up with for derailing the focus of their movement and accusing them of sexism. They see SJWism as a corrosive and corrupting contagion, sullying everything it sets its sights on with its extreme identity politics, culture of victimization, and unwinnable zero-sum conceptions of privilege and oppression that pervade their assessment of everything in the world from Occupy Wall Street to the online atheism movement to astronomer's T-shirts to video games.

Soon, Anita Sarkeesian became the focal point for Gamergater's ire, as her videos (including her other videos in her Feminist Frequency catalogue) were seen as the epitome of what Gamergater's saw as the problem with SJWism. In turn, anti-Gamergaters saw her as the centerpiece figure at the vanguard of their crusade to weed out sexism. Anita Sarkeesian, like Zoe Quinn, was alleged to have received gruesome threats of physical harm and death as a result of her opinions and videos, which anti-Gamergaters again insisted was only because she's a woman stepping on a traditionally male turf.

The mainstream media started to cover this story when it reached critical mass around, I think, autumn-winter 2014. The mainstream media by and large sided with the anti-Gamergaters in their assessment of the Gamergaters as motivated by misogyny and hate - everything from the Guardian to the Telegraph to gaming journalist sites to everything in between with very few exceptions. I suspect the overwhelming one-sidedness was a product of a few things: the difficulty in falsifying claims on either side (e.g. was there actually an ethics problem? Were there actually death threats? Are Gamergaters motivated by sexism?); the difficulty in unravelling the clusterfuck of the very confusing timeline of events; and I think the most compelling reason for the mainstream media's one-sidedness was simply that it's far less risky to side with the people claiming they're being oppressed and harassed. It's more risky to be the one who says "Maybe this is silly and it's all made up oppression politics and victim-seeking."

TL;DR: In 2014, video gamers were upset about alleged ethics issues in gaming journalism; feminists saw this as rooted in sexism and misogyny; months-long battle ensues on social media and general public discourse over whether Gamergate is rooted in sexism and misogyny (having lost sight of the original genesis of the movement); mainstream media started covering it after the battle reached critical mass, and they by-and-large sided with the feminists; shit seems to have died down in 2015. Whole thing was a cluster-quagmire-catastrophuck of epic proportions that split the gaming community down the middle and sent tempers soaring for months and whose ripple effects will be felt for a while I imagine. For reference, Gamergate, or "GG", refers to the anti-bad-ethics-in-journalism movement-turned-anti-SJWism-in-gaming-movement (or anti-women-in-gaming movement, if you believe the SJWs).

ELI5 Version:

Some people were upset about bad video game journalism (Gamergaters). Other people (feminists) thought those GGers were attacking someone out of sexism instead of something else. GGers defended themselves, and ended up becoming anti-feminist.

Now, Gamergate just wants everyone to take a chill pill and enjoy good games for good reasons. Those that are against it want game developers to consider their impact on society seriously instead of doing whatever they think is right.
